title: Who Is Attending Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s Wedding?
summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s top secret wedding. Find out who received an invite.
story: The hottest ticket in Hollywood right now is an invite to Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s top secret wedding.

The highly anticipated nuptials, which Swifites have been theorizing about since the couple got engaged in August 2025, is rumored to be taking place during Independence Day weekend. Speculation has been growing as clues point to the two saying “I do” at Madison Square Garden on Friday, July 3.

A source at the venue, who declined to be identified, told NBC News that MSG has July 2 through July 4 blocked off for a huge event. The source could not confirm that the event involved Swift and Kelce’s nuptials. However, The New York Times first reported that a permit was filed with the city to request street closures surrounding the arena, a crowd for about 500 to 999 people and a tent. Dora Pekec, a spokesperson for the New York City Mayor’s Office, also confirmed these details to NBC News.
That number could be even higher, as a source who landed an invite told NBC News that around 1,100 people are expected to be at the July 3 festivities.
But that’s not all: about 100 will travel to MSG for an intimate ceremony on July 2, the NYT reports. So, who will be on the guest list at one or both events?
Who Is or May Be Attending Taylor and Travis’ Wedding?
Well, only a few celebrities have revealed they received invitations, which were sent electronically with non-disclosure agreements, according to a source who was invited.
Friend Suki Waterhouse, who opened for Swift at one of her London “Eras Tour” dates, let it slip during an interview with Variety in May that she will be going.

Waterhouse was discussing her possible wedding to fiancé Robert Pattinson when she said, “Nothing scarier than the actual planning part, right? I’m gonna go to Taylor’s wedding, and maybe I’ll get some inspiration. It will be amazing.”
San Francisco 49ers star player George Kittle and his wife, Claire, told “Entertainment Tonight” that they already RSVP’d, too. But, he said he has “no idea” where the ceremony will be.

After his wife said she also didn’t know, Kittle added, “I actually asked Travis last night and he laughed at me. I’m half expecting there just to be a jumbo jet on a runway and they put us on a plane somewhere. I don’t have expectations. I know it’s going to be amazing.”
Ahead of the holiday weekend, Rolling Stone reported that Stevie Nicks, Swift’s longtime mentor and friend, will possibly be a guest and a performer.
In October 2025, Swift invited British radio DJ Greg James to the wedding during a BBC Radio 1 interview promoting her “The Life of a Showgirl” album.

When James, who has known Swift for years, joked that he couldn’t wait to meet Kelce for the first time so he could “play catch” with the tight end or “do a wrestling move” with him, she replied, “The way that he’s going to do that as soon as he sees you at our wedding. That’s going to happen.”
James appeared to be shocked and asked, “Am I coming?”
Swift quickly responded, “Obviously.”
The other hundreds of guests are likely to include celebrities, family members and friends.

Jason Kelce will surely be supporting his younger brother, along with wife Kylie Kelce and their four daughters, Wyatt, Ellie, Bennett and Finn. Parents Donna Kelce and Ed Kelce would also be on hand for the special moment.
On the Swift family side, her parents, Andrea and Scott Swift, and younger brother Austin Swift will likely be there.

Many of Kelce’s Kansas City Chiefs teammates, like Patrick Mahomes and wife Brittany, probably made the cut. As well as Swift’s close friends, such as Selena Gomez, Gigi Hadid, HAIM sisters Este, Danielle, and Alana Haim, childhood bestie Abigail Anderson, who could all be in attendance.

title: Taylor Swift’s Parents: What to Know About Scott and Andrea Swift
summary: Taylor Swift parents, Scott and Andrea Swift, have been by her side for every album. Read on to learn about them.
story: Long before Taylor Swift was selling out stadiums, two “Swifties” were sitting in the stands: parents Scott and Andrea Swift.

The mom and dad of the international pop sensation believed in their daughter’s talents from Day 1 and moved their entire family to Nashville more than two decades ago to help her chase her singing and songwriting dreams.
The “Life of a Showgirl” singer has often spoken about how her family’s love has guided her, and she’s thanked them for the sacrifices they’ve made for her career.

After winning top new female vocalist at the 2008 Academy of Country Music Awards, Taylor Swift said, “There are so many people that deserve to be thanked for this,” but she dedicated her acceptance speech to just one: her mom.

“And that’s the person that used to love to go to lunch with her friends and cook dinner for her family and sleep in her bed every night, and she gave that all away and left it all behind to go on the road with her 16-year-old daughter,” Taylor Swift said during the speech, in part. “And so, Mom, thank you so much. I love you. This is for you.”

As Taylor Swift’s success as a crossover artist took on a life of its own, her parents have continued to support her along the way. Scott Swift, 74, and Andrea Swift, 68, have been spotted singing along at their daughter’s concerts, interacting with her devoted fan base and, as of the past couple years, attending NFL games to support Taylor Swift’s beau, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce.
While Taylor Swift’s career has evolved, her love for her family remains consistent. Read on to learn more about Taylor Swift’s parents — her first and strongest supporters.
Who Are Scott and Andrea Swift?

Andrea and Scott Swift tied the knot in 1988, about a year before welcoming their daughter on Dec. 13, 1989. The date is significant to many Swifties as 13 is the singer’s iconic lucky number, and she named her fifth studio album “1989.”
The couple welcomed Taylor Swift’s younger brother, Austin Swift, in 1992.

Taylor Swift isn’t the first musician in Andrea Swift’s bloodline. Andrea Swift is the daughter of American opera singer Marjorie Finaly, who Taylor Swift frequently references, including in her song “Marjorie” on her “Evermore” album.
Andrea Swift also spent some time growing up in Singapore due to her mother’s career, Taylor Swift revealed during her March 2024 “Eras Tour” show in Singapore.

“A lot of the time when we’d come here on tour, my mom would take me and drive me past her old house, where she used to go to school. So, I’ve been hearing about Singapore my whole life,” she said during the show.
Known affectionately to many Swifties as “Mama Swift,” Andrea Swift is frequently seen by her daughter’s side at concerts, award shows and other events, where she is often friendly with fans.
The pop star’s relationship with her mom is shown in a heartwarming compilation of images and videos from her childhood in the official video for her song “The Best Day (Taylor’s Version).”
“You’re the prettiest lady in the whole wide world,” she sings on the song. “I love you for giving me your eyes.”
In the song, Taylor Swift also mentions her love for her father.
“I have an excellent father,” she sings. “His strength is making me stronger.”

Scott Swift has worked as a financial advisor at Merrill Lynch and later established Swift Group. Though he’s clearly got a head for business, the proud dad also likes to let loose, as evidenced in a playful TikTok video of him riding a Segway that his daughter posted during her “Eras Tour.”
They Moved From Pennsylvania to Tennessee
Taylor Swift shared another compilation of family images and videos in her official video for the 2019 holiday tune “Christmas Tree Farm.”
Taylor Swift alludes in the song to the Christmas tree farm where she was raised.
The singer and her brother were both born in Reading, Pennsylvania, and in 2003, their parents moved the whole family to Nashville to support Swift’s singing career.
“At 13, I was offered a development deal by a major record label,” Taylor Swift told Time in 2014.
“My parents gave in and we moved from Pennsylvania (to Nashville),” she added.

After Taylor Swift announced the release of “Speak Now (Taylor’s Version)” in Nashville during “The Eras Tour,” she reflected on how she felt when first writing the album between the ages of 18 and 20 while living in the nostalgia-filled city.
“The songs that came from this time in my life were marked by their brutal honesty, unfiltered diaristic confessions and wild wistfulness,” she wrote.

At the reception for her induction into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in June 2026, Taylor Swift thanked her parents and brother once again for their early leap of faith: “It was easy to choose songwriting over everything else in my life, but it couldn’t have been easy for my parents and my brother to just pick up and move our entire family from Pennsylvania to relocate to Nashville so that I could hone my craft in the songwriting capital of the world.”
Through tears, she added, “Even though words are supposed to kind of be my thing, I will never be able to express my gratitude to you guys for doing that for me. You’re the reason I’m here today.”
Scott and Andrea Swift’s Cancer Journeys
Both Andrea and Scott Swift have been diagnosed with cancer in the past, Taylor Swift revealed in a 2019 essay for Elle.
“I’ve had to learn how to handle serious illness in my family,” she wrote. “Both of my parents have had cancer, and my mom is now fighting her battle with it again.”
Taylor Swift revealed that her mother was battling cancer in 2015, then again in 2019, though she did not share the type of the cancer at the time.
The singer has shared her distress over her mom’s diagnosis through her music.
“Who am I supposed to talk to? What am I supposed to do if there’s no you,” she sang in her 2019 track “Soon You’ll Get Better.”
“You’ll get better soon, ‘cause you have to,” she sang.
In a 2019 interview with CBS News, she said she “can’t even listen to” the song.
“I don’t think I have written a song quite like that before,” she said. “It’s just not something we deal with until we have to. Writing about it was really emotional.”
She performed the song live for the first time in August 2019.
In 2020, Taylor shared that her mother was diagnosed with a brain tumor.
She told Variety that her mother was diagnosed with the tumor while undergoing chemotherapy treatments for cancer.
Scott Swift Almost Inspired Taylor Swift to Pursue a Different Career

When Taylor Swift was only 8 years old, she didn’t know she was destined for music stardom. Instead, she thought she’d go a much more corporate route, she revealed during a 2011 “YouTube Presents” interview.

“Ever since I was, like, 8 years old, my dad has been telling me to save my money or invest in utilities,” then-21-year-old Taylor Swift said. “My dad is so passionate about what he does in the way that I’m so passionate about music. This guy lives for being a stockbroker.”

So, when people would ask young Taylor Swift what she wanted to be when she grew up, her answer was paternally inspired: “I didn’t know what a stockbroker was when I was 8, but I would just tell everybody that’s what I was going to be. It would be, like [the] first day of school, and they’re like, ‘So what do you want to be when you grow up?’ And everybody is [like], ‘I want to be an astronaut’ or ‘I want to be a ballerina.’ And I’m like, ‘I want to be a financial advisor.’”
While crunching numbers doesn’t typically excite an elementary school student, her dad’s love for his work made it appealing, the singer explained.
“I love my dad so much, because he’s so gung-ho for his job, and I just thought how happy it made him, and I just thought, ‘I can broke stocks,’” Taylor Swift said.
Scott Swift’s Political Disagreements With His Daughter
The 2020 Netflix documentary “Miss Americana” showed Taylor Swift and her father having political disagreements.
Taylor Swift decided to voice her political opinions on social media, a choice her father didn’t agree with at the time. In 2018, she released a lengthy statement on Instagram.
She said she does not support Marsha Blackburn running for Senate in the state of Tennessee, saying she “votes against equal pay for women,” and the “Violence Against Women Act.”
“These are not MY Tennessee values,” she wrote.
The documentary shows her father saying he was “terrified” about Taylor Swift sharing her political views.
Taylor Swift went through with the post.
“I need to do this,” she told her father. “Dad, I need you to forgive me for doing this, because I’m doing it.”
Andrea and Scott Swift at ‘The Eras Tour’
From day one to today, the star’s parents have publicly supported her career.
On the North American leg of “The Eras Tour,” Andrea and Scott Swift attended many of the shows.
One TikTok user posted a video in May 2023 which shows the two at her show in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
Andrea and Scott Swift are seen in the video walking into the venue together while fans gift them friendship bracelets — a tradition created during the “Eras Tour.”
Another TikTok video, posted in July 2023, shows the two inside the VIP tent at their daughter’s show in Seattle, Washington.
Both Andrea and Scott Swift are seen singing along as their daughter performs her track “You Belong With Me.” At one point, Scott Swift takes out his phone to record his daughter’s performance.

At multiple “Eras Tour” shows, Scott Swift —a longstanding NFL fan — was also seen in the crowd accompanied by Travis Kelce, including at the Nov. 11, 2023, show in Argentina and the Feb. 23, 2024, concert in Sydney, Australia.
Taylor Swift’s Parents Have Joined Her at Multiple Kansas City Chiefs Games

The singer’s parents have both been spotted at plenty of Chiefs games, including at the team’s Nov. 29, 2024, Black Friday game. Scott Swift was photographed arriving at Arrowhead Stadium with his daughter, as well as Kelce’s mom, Donna.
After the team defeated the San Francisco 49ers to win the Super Bowl in February 2024, Taylor Swift posted a funny TikTok of her parents celebrating the win at an after party.
“Accidentally going clubbing with your parents is something everyone should try at least once in their life,” she captioned the post.

The singer also brought her parents and brother along to watch the Chiefs claim victory over the the Buffalo Bills in the 2025 AFC championship, which advanced Kansas City its third Super Bowl in a row.
Scott Swift Underwent Major Open Heart Surgery
During her feature on Kelce’s “New Heights” podcast in August 2025, Taylor Swift revealed that her dad underwent a surprise quintuple bypass surgery after a stress test uncovered serious blockages.

The singer said the surgery — which involves creating new routes, or “bypasses,” for blood and oxygen to reach the heart, per the National Library of Medicine — came as a shock, as her father had shown no signs of trouble during previous EKG exams.
Scott Swift insisted that his kids don’t take time out of their busy lives to attend to him, and even humorously compared his ability to heal alone to that of a cat.
“He said something about like when a cat is injured it curls up around a tree and heals itself, I was like ‘Dad, cats don’t have quintuple bypass surgery,’” Taylor Swift said.
But despite his wishes, Andrea, Taylor and Austin Swift were all in the waiting room alongside Scott Swift’s best friend when he woke up from surgery, Taylor Swift said.

She described the entire situation as “parent-child reversal” — from confiscating his phone so he would rest to assembling his wheelchair and other recovery aids, just like he assembled her play sets and swing sets.
That same summer, Andrea Swift also had knee surgery, Taylor Swift added during the podcast.
“This was just like the summer of my parental upgrades,” she joked.
The following December, Taylor Swift donated $1 million to the American Heart Association, supporting a cause that had gained new meaning for the family.
Andrea Swift Encouraged Taylor Swift to Give Travis Kelce a Chance

After Kelce expressed his interest in meeting Taylor Swift during a July 2023 episode of his New Heights podcast, Andrea Swift was interested in learning more about the athlete, she recalled during Episode 4 of Taylor Swift’s “The End of An Era” docuseries on Disney+.
So, Andrea Swift did some digging, and she contacted her “resident expert on [the] Kansas City Chiefs”: her cousin Robin.
Robin told her that Kelce is “the nicest guy” and “really loves his mom,” Andrea recalled. “And I went, ding, ding, ding, ding. Then I said, ‘Now how in the world am I going to get her to meet him?’”
After some light persuasion, battling against the pop star’s initial resistance to dating athletes, the efforts paid off.
“Listen, it was so earnest. I thought it was the sweetest thing in the world that he came to your show. He brought you something from your world. To me, that really said a lot,” Andrea Swift said.

She shared further adoration for her daughter’s then-boyfriend during the doc: “He really is one of the happiest people I think I’ve ever met, which I adore. He just brought a lot of happiness, which is I think what he does in a lot of his circles. He brings a lot of happiness to the world.”
Andrea Swift Played a Key Role Helping Taylor Swift Buy Her Music
During her “New Heights” appearance, Taylor Swift also recalled how she entrusted her mother and brother to facilitate the deal with private equity firm Shamrock Capitol to buy her music catalogue.

“They sat down with Shamrock Capital and told them what this meant to me,” Taylor Swift said. “They told them the whole story of all the times we’ve tried to buy it, of all the times it’s fallen through, all the times we had gotten plans together and figured out something we thought was gonna work and it didn’t at the last minute.”
When Taylor Swift finally got the call from her mother confirming that she and Austin Swift had secured the deal, the singer said she burst into tears.

title: Anna McCallie’s Debut Romance, ‘Abby Offsides,’ Started as a Bedtime Story She Told Herself to Fall Asleep
summary: Anna McCallie joins Jenna Bush Hager on Open Book with Jenna in an episode out July 2.
story: London-based novelist Anna McCallie made her authorial debut on June 23 with “Abby Offsides,” a rom-com about a woman who abruptly ends her engagement, moves across the pond and falls in love with Lachlan Ramsay, a Scottish soccer star.
The novel, fit for the World Cup obsessed, is the latest book from Jenna Bush Hager’s imprint, Thousand Voices x Random House Publishing Group.
During the July 2 episode of “Open Book with Jenna,” McCallie told Jenna about the surprising origins of the tale.
“Abby Offsides” started as a story McCallie told in her head to fall asleep at night. The only issue is that Abby’s love story quickly started to keep McCallie up.

“I just thought to myself, ‘All right, I’m going to imagine a woman, and I’m going to just think about the mundane details of her life. What does her hair look like? What’s she wearing? What does her office look like?’ And try to have it be just exciting enough that it drowned out the other thoughts, but not so exciting that I was staying up thinking about her,” McCallie said.
It didn’t take long before that plan unraveled.

“Unfortunately, I failed, and she became too exciting, because night after night she ended up at a club with a man, and there was something wrong about it, and I just kept coming back to it,” the author told Jenna.
Then, McCallie decided to confide in a friend about her nightly issue.

“I was telling my friend how I’ve totally failed at this insomnia cure, and he was like, ‘Yeah, that’s because you’re writing a book.’ I just hadn’t even thought of turning it into a story. As soon as he said it, I just thought, ‘Oh my God, he’s right,’ and so I started writing it down,” she said.
More about 'Abby Offsides'
‘Abby Offsides’, the Latest Book from Jenna’s Imprint, Is a Rom-Com for the World Cup-Obsessed
‘Abby Offsides’, the Latest Book from Jenna’s Imprint, Is a Rom-Com for the World Cup-Obsessed
Abby and Lachlan’s love story interfered with Jenna’s sleep schedule, too, she told McCallie.

“I remember where I was when I finished (‘Abby Offsides’), because I was in bed with my own husband, and I was like, ‘No more noise,’ because I was so invested in these characters,” Jenna said, laughing. “I think sometimes creating a world where people want to stay up late into night, ‘flashlight reading,’ is because you yourself were sort of not burdened by the story, but overcome with it.”

That “flashlight reading” is one of McCallie’s “favorite experiences as a reader,” she told Jenna. Having come up with the U.K. soccer romance herself, she didn’t get to have the same experience with the story, she said.
Still, McCallie said it’s exciting her first novel can do that for other readers.

“I’m so in the weeds that I don’t know what it was like to fall in love with Lachlan, because I was creating him,” she said. “I love the idea that people are up there turning pages way past their bedtime … it’s totally surreal that I have now created that experience for other people.”

title: So, How Much Does A Wedding At Madison Square Garden Actually Cost?
summary: TODAY.com spoke to luxury wedding planners and event experts to get their take on how much a wedding at Madison Square Garden, like that of Swift, would cost.
story: With Taylor Swift’s wedding of the century rumored to be held at New York City’s famed Madison Square Garden this summer, the question remains: What’s the price tag on a wedding at the World’s Most Famous Arena?

TODAY.com spoke to luxury wedding planners and event experts, who’ve had experience with organizing some of the most opulent parties and nuptials, to get their take on how much a MSG wedding could cost. While it’s impossible to pinpoint an exact number without details on guest count, decor and more, experts say the ballpark costs are, unsurprisingly, a pretty penny.
“You’re not getting out alive for under $15 million to $25 million,” estimates Alyssa Pettinato, founder of New York–based luxury wedding planning and event design firm Alinato Events.

Though details have yet to be confirmed, developments appear to support the rumor that Swift and Travis Kelce will have their big day at the Garden. A source at the venue, who declined to be identified to discuss the confidential matter, told NBC News that the arena has been blocked off from July 2 through July 4 for an event. Dora Pekec, a spokesperson for the New York City Mayor’s Office, also confirmed to NBC News that a permit filed with the city, as first reported by The New York Times, requested street closures near the arena, a crowd between 500 and 999 people and a tent set up outside.

Others who want to get married at the legendary arena may be in for some sticker shock. According to the MSG website, the venue is available to rent for events that call “for a space unmatched in scale, history and excitement.” The arena itself can hold up to 19,500 guests. Other areas of the Garden are also available for rent, including its famed theater and exclusive clubs and lounges. Wedding planners estimate that the space alone will skyrocket the budget into the millions.

Madison Square Garden did not respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment. Representatives for Kelce and Swift have not responded to requests for comment and confirmation about reported wedding details.
The Venue

A source with knowledge of the matter, who is among the invitees, told NBC News that Swift and Kelce’s wedding festivities  at Madison Square Garden on July 3 are expected to have more than 1,000 attendees.

Ashley Smith, owner and creative director of luxury planning and design company Ashley Smith Events, explains that the couple would typically need to rent out the space not only for the day of the wedding ceremony and festivities, but also for the days surrounding the event to allow for the venue’s transformation. There’s often an insurance fee as well, Smith says.

Venues as large as the Garden also often come with preferred vendors and unionized labor for staging, lighting and other crew, she says. And if the couple has their own crew and vendors in mind, they’d have to buy out the Garden’s own people.
Both Pettinato and Smith say single-day rental fees for the Garden range upwards of $1 million to $2 million, meaning the cost of the venue alone could reach $8 million to $10 million.

“It might be something like a three or four day buyout of Madison Square Garden,” Smith says. “If we’re talking multiple days and all the factors that go into it, (cost) starts to creep up really fast.”
The Decor

Beyond the venue itself, couples also would have to budget for the costs of decor. And MSG has quite a wealth of space that needs to be transformed, Pettinato says. Decor alone, both experts say, could reach the $20 million mark.

“We have to think about it like this: How tall is Madison Square Garden? How high is that ceiling from the floor?” Pettinato says. “If you’re trying to put something that’s going to cover some of these more gaudy aspects of it, you’ve got to get a crane in there.”

As of June 30, crews were photographed outside of the Garden, unloading trucks and moving around large items under tarps and black garbage bags. One crew member was seen wearing a “Taylor Swift Carpenters” shirt.
Smith says that cavernous spaces generally require much more decoration and treatments to make the space feel personal. Oftentimes, scenic walls are created to do so.

“If they’re going to divvy up that space, you create faux walls,” Smith says. “There’s a lot of draping, covering the ceiling, those types of things so that we’re not seeing all the big heavy equipment in there.”
The Security

One of the biggest expenses for celebrities and any high profile figures who have weddings at such major venues is security, Pettinato and Smith say. A source among those invited told NBC News that guests received electronic invites along with non-disclosure agreements. But Pettinato says the couple’s security likely doesn’t stop with NDAs. Securing the area would likely cost around $1 million to $2 million a day, she says.

“A private security company, often with former political security people, is expensive for those skills,” Pettinato says. “If you’re using them for multiple days to secure a site, and also monitor every single piece of it, from who comes in to what everyone’s doing in that room … It’s an operation.”
Pettinato says she once planned a wedding that was attended by a Supreme Court justice. The justice’s presence necessitated a sweep of the area, weeks before the event.
“They even had me explain the type of flowers (at the wedding) so that they could know what was being put in front of the Supreme Court justice in case it was laced with poison,” she says.
Security for these major events, Pettinato says, often ends up being one of the biggest expenses.
More Potential Costs

The costs, of course, don’t stop there. There’s also food, which can cost around $600 a head for a three-course meal, Smith says. So for a 200-person wedding, catering and beverage costs can total more than $100,000. Swift’s wedding is expected to have many more guests — around 1,100 people at the festivities on July 3, the invited source told NBC News.

Entertainment fees are astronomical as well, depending on who is performing. So far, Stevie Nicks, whom Swift has performed with in the past, is rumored to be playing at the wedding, according to Rolling Stone. According to a celebrity booking agency, her fee can start at around $2 million.
So Who Gets To Have A Wedding At The Garden?
Unsurprisingly, weddings at a venue like the Garden are rare, and likely only attainable to those who can easily spend upwards of $10 million, Smith says.

There have been just two known weddings at the venue. The first was between musician Sly Stone and model Kathy Silva, who got married at the Garden in 1974 during one of his concerts. According to the New York Times, the ceremony involved a full wedding party, including the couple’s four parents, and took place in front of 23,000 fans. Later on, a more private reception of 400 people was held at the Waldorf-Astoria.

The other ceremony was a 1982 mass wedding of 2,075 couples performed by Rev. Sun Myung Moon of the controversial Unification Church, often referred to as the “Moonies.” Couples, dressed in identical blue suits and wedding dresses made by the church, had their nuptials on the arena’s floor, which was carpeted in all white, according to the Times.

title: USWNT Star Lily Yohannes Says This Career Moment Is One She ‘Will Never Forget’
summary: USWNT star Lily Yohannes shares her favorite World Cup memory and career moment that she is most proud of.
story: Lily Yohannes can “vividly” remember the feeling she had after making her debut with the United States Women’s National Team.
“I came on for, like, maybe 10 minutes and then I scored,” the 19-year-old Adidas athlete tells TODAY.com.

The unforgettable moment came during the USWNT’s match against Korea Republic on June 4, 2024. Two years later, Yohannes continues to score goals as a midfielder for the French Première Ligue club OL Lyonnes.
This summer, she’s “cheering on the boys” of the United States Men’s National Team as they host the 2026 FIFA World Cup alongside Mexico and Canada.
“Watching these games on home soil is super special,” she says, adding it’s exciting to see soccer legends like Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi in cities they might never have played before.
Below, in her own words, Yohannes shares her World Cup memories, insight into how she knew she wanted to play soccer and more.
(It would be in 2015). I remember jumping up and down in front of the TV (when) Carli Lloyd (scored) the goal from half field (during the Women’s World Cup final).

I don’t think it’s one moment. As a kid you watch these players playing on the stage in a World Cup and you just dream of achieving the same, of being in that position. For me, it’s always been a dream of mine and now to be on the national team and playing professionally, it’s so amazing — and hopefully one day playing at a World Cup.

My family has been there for me, since, forever. Everything that they do for me, sacrificed since I was a little kid, my parents have always put me first to help me chase my dreams and be in the position I am today. They’re my biggest fans, my biggest champions.

I would say my debut for the national team. That was just such a special moment, and a moment that I will never forget. I can feel it vividly, see the moment happening now to this day. It’s a dream just to play for the national team and to make your debut, it made me feel so honored, grateful and just so excited.

I came on for, like, maybe 10 minutes and then I scored. (I felt) all the emotions, running to celebrate, the team coming to embrace me just made the moment that much more special. It’s just a moment that you work for your whole life and to have that moment to celebrate it with my teammates, with my family who have supported me the whole way, was incredible.

title: Liz McGraw Steps Away from ‘Real Housewives of Rhode Island’ Season 2
summary: But she is, ma. Liz McGraw will step away from “Real Housewives of Rhode Island” for Season 2, after quickly becoming a fan favorite for her teasing confessionals and zippy one-liners.
story: But she is, ma. Liz McGraw will step away from “Real Housewives of Rhode Island” for Season 2, after quickly becoming a fan favorite for her teasing confessionals and zippy one-liners.
Liz on July 1 announced her departure from the reality TV show on Instagram, writing that she plans to “focus on my family, my work and my passions.”
“As filming for Season 2 begins, I have made the decision to take a step back,” she said in her statement.
She added that she’s “full of gratitude” for her time as a main cast member and will be watching the next season.
TODAY.com has reached out to Bravo for comment but did not immediately hear back. The network’s official Instagram commented a heart emoji on Liz’s post.
“Real Housewives of Rhode Island” premiered in April and aired a two-part reunion on June 21 and June 28. The Bravo show was renewed for a second season in May.

Liz, 56, is described in the show as Rhode Island’s “Cannabis Queen.” She owns and operates the state’s largest cannabis dispensary. Liz is married to Gerry McGraw and stepmother to his three children. She’s longtime friends with “Real Housewives of New Jersey” star Dolores Catania, who made several appearances throughout “Rhode Island’s” debut season.

Liz was represented as one of the leaders of the “Real Housewives of Rhode Island” group throughout Season 1, with longtime friendships with Kelsey Swanson, Alicia Carmody and Jo-Ellen Tiberi. Over Season 1’s 12 episodes, tension escalated between Liz and Jo-Ellen before exploding at a brunch outing. During the reunion, Liz questioned Jo-Ellen’s description of their relationship as “best friends.”
The cast for Season 2 of “RHORI” is unclear. Season 1 featured Liz, Kelsey, Alicia, Jo-Ellen as well as Rosie DiMare, Rulla Nehme Pontarelli and “Bachelor” franchise alum Ashley Iaconetti.

title: William Daniels Celebrates 75 Years of Marriage with Bonnie Bartlett. What’s the Key to Their Love Story?
summary: William Daniels and Bonnie Bartlett are celebrating 75 years of marriage together. They share some of the ways they’ve made it work.
story: William Daniels and Bonnie Bartlett are celebrating 75 years of marriage.
The “Boy Meets World” actor celebrated the occasion with a photo of the couple shared to Facebook on June 30.

“Happy 75th Anniversary to my wife Bonnie. It doesn’t even seem that long it just seems like this is my life. And it’s with each other. How lucky am I?” he captioned the post, which included a picture of Daniels sitting in a chair while Bartlett stands over him with her hands on his chest.
Daniels, who turned 99 in March, met Bartlett, who turned 97 in June, while they were both students at Northwestern University.
“Well, we’ve been together actually 78 years because it was three years in college,” Bartlett told Page Six in a joint interview in May.
What’s the Key to Their Marriage?
When you’ve been married as long as Daniels and Bartlett have, people are bound to wonder how they make it work. So, what is the key to their success?
“Life is all adjustment. You’re constantly adjusting,” Bartlett told Page Six.

“It suddenly got hot here (in Los Angeles), and it got hard to breathe and to move around. You have to kind of adjust to the heat,” she added. “And that’s what life’s all about — is adjusting to whatever your circumstances are and however you move along. And certainly a marriage is full of adjustments.”
Bartlett says Daniels is often approached about advice about marriage. What does he say when people ask him?
“Don’t!” he joked.
The Couple Emphasizes Caring
Daniels and Bartlett have worked with each other over the years, including playing spouses on “Boy Meets World” and “St. Elsewhere,” for which they each won a pair of Emmys.
Bartlett says marriage is a two-way street.

“Caring about your happiness, yes. You’ve got to be happy, too, but caring about the other person’s happiness. Being patient if there’s some kind of a problem that you’re going through, being very caring and very helpful,” she told People in 2024.
They Embrace Surprises
She also said that Daniels can still catch her off-guard.

“Every once in a while, he’ll do something, and I think, ‘Where did that come from? Where did that come from?’ Or, he the same with me,” she told People. “We never stop being surprised by what somebody does.”
They Survived a Rocky Period of Their Marriage
Daniels and Bartlett had an open marriage early on in their union. The two wed in 1951.

“It was non-spoken,” Bartlett told the Daily Mail in May. “Bill and I never sit down and make rules. We never sit down and talk about these things. We just don’t. We just live our lives. And if he’s away for a year, he’s away for a year.”
“Our lives just went on, but we never got unhinged… We never got unhinged, but our lives did go in different directions occasionally,” she added.

“I guess it was a little bit of an open marriage at first, but that was very painful,” she told Fox News in 2023. “That didn’t work well. And it was a time when people were doing that. It was at a time in New York when there was a lot of sex and a lot of people doing all kinds of things, you know — very free.
“But I don’t know if there was a lack of commitment a little bit, and that’s not good,” she added. “So there was a lot of pain connected with any transgression, with any extramarital thing.”
They Adore Their Two Children
Bartlett and Daniels are also parents to two sons, Michael and Robert, whom they adopted after their son William Jr. died as a newborn in 1961.

“That’s the best thing that ever happened to us. And it happened after losing a child, after great pain and sadness, and then we got these two wonderful boys, and they have been a joy the whole marriage. I can’t imagine life without them,” she told People in 2024.

title: All of Taylor Swift’s Lyrics About Getting Married, From ‘Love Story’ to ‘Honey’
summary: Taylor Swift’s wedding to NFL tight end Travis Kelce seems to be coming on the July 4 weekend. Here are all her lyrics that reference marriage and weddings.
story: Taylor Swift’s highly anticipated wedding to NFL tight end Travis Kelce seems to be coming on the July 4 weekend. Many are calling this pairing America’s equivalent to a royal wedding. Are you ready for it?

While no wedding details have been officially confirmed by Swift or Kelce, a source with knowledge of the matter, who is among the guests invited, told NBC News that 1,100 people are expected to attend wedding festivities on July 3 at Madison Square Garden. A spokesperson with the New York City Mayor’s Office also confirmed that a permit was filed requesting street closures around the arena for July 2 through 4.

Swift’s actual wedding may be shrouded in mystery, but the singer has often referenced weddings and marriage in her songs, including the epic proposal at the end of “Love Story” and her apparent rejection of tradition in lyrics throughout “Midnights.” Swift has said her lyrics can range from deeply personal, as she explained to Glamour in 2012, to fictional, like with “Folklore” and “Evermore.”

In honor of Swift and Kelce, who announced their engagement in August 2025, possibly sharing more than paper rings later this week, here’s a Swiftie-certified look back on the biggest references to marriage from her 13-album discography.
Song: “Mary’s Song (Oh My My My)”
Album: “Taylor Swift” (2006)
From her very first studio album, Swift was seemingly already envisioning what her proposal could look like. Per photos shared in August 2025, Kelce proposed to Swift in a flower garden in Missouri.
Song: “Love Story”
Album: “Fearless” (2008)
“Love Story” describes Swift meeting her “Romeo” and overcoming conflict for a heroic proposal where she has to “just say yes.” Luckily for Kelce, she did!
Song: “Fifteen”
Album: “Fearless” (2008)

On the same 2008 album as “Love Story,” Swift sings about teen heartbreak and moving on from dreams of marriage for other horizons. Swift won her first Grammy Awards for “Fearless” in 2010, including best female country vocal performance, best country album and the night’s highest prize, album of the year.
Song: “Speak Now”
Album: “Speak Now” (2010)
This title track for Swift’s third album imagines its narrator making one last effort to confess her feelings to someone she loves — by interrupting their wedding.
Song: “Starlight”
Album: “Red” (2012)

Unlike most of Swift’s songs, we know exactly who inspired this track: Robert F. Kennedy and Ethel Kennedy. She said she saw a photo of them together aged 17 and dreamed up a version of their romance. But at least one lyric rings true. They did get married and go on to have many, many children.
Song: “Lover”
Album: “Lover” (2019)

In this title track that soon became a popular wedding anthem, Swift cites a line often said by a wedding officiant during the ceremony before issuing her personalized vows. But instead of taking the subject to be her husband, she pronounces him her “lover.”
Song: “Paper Rings”
Album: “Lover” (2019)

“Paper Rings” declares that its narrator doesn’t need a diamond to make things official. (Swift’s fiancé, though, had other plans. He proposed with a brilliant cushion cut old mine diamond, estimated to be worth between $500,000 and $1 million.)
Song: “My Tears Ricochet”
Album: “Folklore” (2020)

This reference to a diamond engagement ring takes a starkly different tone than past songs. Instead of celebrating romance, “My Tears Ricochet” is about divorce and, in Swift’s words, realizing that a “person that you trusted more than anyone in the world is the person that can hurt you the worst.”
Song: “Champagne Problems”
Album: “Evermore” (2020)

Like “My Tears Ricochet,” “Champagne Problems” was written amid the COVID-19 pandemic and Swift’s shift to fictional storytelling in her music. This song follows a young woman who turns down a proposal, aware she’s breaking someone’s heart but unable to say yes.
Song: “I Bet You Think About Me”
Album: “Red (Taylor’s Version)” (2021)

While the lyrics don’t explicitly reference marriage, the music video for this “Red” vault track depicts Swift haunting a wedding of an apparent ex (played by Miles Teller). She pops up dressed in red as a wallflower attendee, a speech-giver and someone sitting at the kid’s table. But halfway through the video, Swift appears in all white and dances with Teller, who seems to be imagining her as his bride. When the illusion breaks, Swift continues her country crooning about being impossible to forget.
Song: “Lavender Haze”
Album: “Midnights” (2022)
In this song, the narrator sings about wanting to stay in a shielded, private “Lavender Haze,” away from tabloids and gossip. These lyrics seemingly shut down speculation over her marital status.
Song: “Midnight Rain”
Album: “Midnights” (2022)
“Midnight Rain” is an illustration of two people with contrasting values and priorities. One wants it “comfortable” while the narrator was “chasing that fame.”
Song: “High Infidelity”
Album: “Midnights” (2022)

This song seemingly centers on a relationship marred by infidelity, with the repeated question: “Do you really wanna know where I was April 29?” The lyric referencing a wedding appears to describe a marriage that was doomed from the start.
Song: “You’re Losing Me”
Album: “Midnights (The Late Night Edition)” (2023)

This song was originally available exclusively on CD and sold during “The Eras Tour” before later being released on streaming. This song describes a relationship slowly dying. Swift’s friend and collaborator Jack Antonoff said the track was written and recorded all in one night, on Dec. 5, 2021.
Song: “The Tortured Poets Department”
Album: “The Tortured Poets Department” (2024)

Here, the narrator recalls a deeply intimate relationship and a moment when they imagined being married — “the closest I’ve come to my heart exploding.” The song overall asks its subject, “Who’s gonna hold you like me? Who’s gonna know you, if not me?”
Song: “But Daddy I Love Him”
Album: “The Tortured Poets Department” (2024)

In this track, the narrator outlines the freedom of being loud and proud about a love that others judge. Throughout the song, she breaks the fourth wall, seemingly addressing listeners and fans directly with, “I’m having his baby/ No, I’m not, but you should see your faces.”
Song: “Fresh Out The Slammer”
Album: “The Tortured Poets Department” (2024)

Like the album’s title track, this song describes a relationship that involved fantasizing about getting married one day. Only in this song, she’s “running back” to that relationship, rather than reflecting on its end.
Song: “Loml”
Album: “The Tortured Poets Department” (2024)

This song, the title of which can refer to both the “love of my life” and the “loss of my life,” is a reflection on the end of a relationship that seemed to be endgame, with promises of marriage and kids.
Song: “Imgonnagetyouback”
Album: “The Tortured Poets Department” (2024)
In this track, Swift depicts two contrasting ends of an emotional spectrum, one of which is possible wife status.
Song: “So High School”
Album: “The Tortured Poets Department” (2024)

This track describes a relationship that feels like, well, high school. The narrator brings up the juvenile game “marry, kiss, kill” and says she’s “betting on all three.” (Of note, in 2016, Kelce was asked that question among Swift, Katy Perry and Ariana Grande. He said he’d kiss Swift.)
Song: “Wi$h Li$t”
Album: “The Life of a Showgirl” (2025)

Swift outlines other people’s ambitions for wealth and fame, from yacht life to a professional soccer contract. The narrator, however, just wants to get married, have kids and put a basketball hoop in their driveway.
Song: “Wood”
Album: “The Life of a Showgirl” (2025)
This bold song is as explicitly suggestive as Swift gets with her lyrics. The narrator of this song is not only sexually satisfied, but knows an engagement ring is soon in her future.
Song: “Honey”
Album: “The Life of a Showgirl” (2025)
In “Honey,” the narrator again describes a simple and sweet domestic life, with “forever night stand” implying marriage and commitment.

title: ‘Love Island USA’ Season 8 Movie Night Brings Lies and a Cliffhanger: Breaking Down the Drama

And the singles are…

KC’s decision to bring Casa Amor bombshell Titi to the villa upset the balance, essentially creating a boys vs. girls dynamic. That tension was heightened during Movie Night in Episode 25, where the islanders watched clips of some of the comments and actions that have occurred throughout the season.

A few standout moments were Aniya seeing KC refer to her as a “grandma,” the girls celebrating Aniya and Carl’s blossoming connection and all the islanders being stunned at how Sincere pursued Sol before she left the villa.
TODAY.com’s Season 8 commentators Tess Higgins and Sally Darr Griffin both approve of the change to the typical Movie Night format.

“Normally, there will be little titles for the clips they’re about to play. There are no titles this year, it’s just doors. And it’s not just clips that they’re watching. They are full-on compilations that have a clear beginning, middle and end to them, which I think hits harder than just a single clip,” Tess notes.

Sally Darr appreciated that the clips helped Kayda realize Alannah, who was removed from the villa after a video resurfaced of her using a racial slur while singing a song, did not participate in the Casa Amor recoupling.

“While I think Zach still would have chosen Kayda even if Alannah had been there for the recoupling, it’s strange that he never told her,” Sally Darr explains. “I suspected Zach hadn’t mentioned it, so I’m glad she finally knows now. Zach not telling Kayda was silly and has only made things worse.”
Read on to find out what Tess and Sally Darr thought about the islanders’ reaction to Part 1 of “Movie Night” and who they think is at risk of being dumped next.
Best Moment

Tess: “The best moment is watching Aniya and Melanie be there for each other, whether that’s like tonight in Movie Night or a couple episodes ago after the Casa recoupling. I’ve really enjoyed seeing their friendship develop and grow as the season’s gone on. Tonight when Melanie said she was shaking during Movie Night, and she wanted to hold Aniya’s hand, and she was there for her giving her the pep talk, I actually teared up a little bit. I thought it was so sweet, and it really goes to show that at the end of the day it kind of is ‘Friendship Island.’”

Sally Darr: “The best moment was Sincere’s Movie Night compilation. KC’s compilation was satisfying, too, but his Casa Amor behavior happened much more recently. Sincere lying to Melanie and Sol happened weeks ago, so revisiting it felt necessary.”
Biggest Surprise

Tess: “On a small scale, the biggest surprise was the editors leaving in two clips, following each other, of Sincere saying ‘beloved’ to both Melanie and Sol. I thought that was really funny. But I’m also surprised with the way that they went about structuring Movie Night. Normally, there will be little titles for the clips they’re about to play. There are no titles this year, it’s just doors. And it’s not just clips that they’re watching. They are full-on compilations that have a clear beginning, middle and end to them, which I think hits harder than just a single clip. And we’re not even halfway through. There is still a cliffhanger and more scenes to come, which I cannot wait to see.”

Sally Darr: The biggest surprise was Kayda finding out that Alannah left in the middle of Casa Amor. While I think Zach still would have chosen Kayda even if Alannah had been there for the recoupling, it’s strange that he never told her. I suspected Zach hadn’t mentioned it, so I’m glad she finally knows now. Zach not telling Kayda was silly and has only made things worse. It’s very short-sighted of him, since Kayda was always going to find out once she left the villa anyway.”
Best Couple

Tess: “The best couple for me is still Bryce and Trinity. They are so easy to root for. I loved seeing their date this week. Finally, we got a date! There have been no dates this season, except for the very first bombshell date. They’re already boyfriend and girlfriend, they skipped over the classic ‘Love Island’ step of closing off before getting to the boyfriend and girlfriend, which I think is really fun. But I do think that Carl and Aniya could catch up to them if they continue on this path with their connection, because it seems very sweet and genuine so far, and something that we would all want to root for, too.”
Sally Darr: “The best couple is Trinity and Bryce. They are going to win this season.”
Biggest Winner

Tess: “The biggest winner has to be Aniya. She has finally seen through all of the nonsense with KC and is able to start something fresh with Carl, who I think is a much better fit for her. It was really hard to watch her feel all that visceral sadness and emotion after the recoupling after Casa. So, I’m glad that she’s past that and able to continue on this new path with someone else.”

Sally Darr: “The biggest winner is Melanie. Even though she’s upset after watching Sincere’s compilation, she now knows she isn’t crazy. I hope she finally sees that Sincere doesn’t respect her, and ends things for good. She’s better off alone.”
At Risk of Being Dumped

Tess: “At risk of being dumped, I think, is most likely Corbin and Parmida, because I’m just not seeing a lot of people really root for them online. I think people don’t see Corbin as a positive influence in the villa, and Parmida, I don’t think is really resonating with viewers either. But I could also see KC and Titi getting the axe soon as well, because no one really wants to root for KC after everything that went down with Aniya. So, I guess one of those couples, or the individuals in those couples, might be going next.”

Sally Darr: “Jen is at risk of being dumped. She’s coupled up with Gal, but they’re no longer getting to know each other. Meanwhile, Gal is talking to Amora, which leaves Jen as the only single person in the villa right now.”

title: In ‘Elle,’ We Meet the Woman Who Made Elle Woods: Her Mother
summary: June Diane Raphael speaks about creating Eva, the mother of Elle Woods in the prequel series Elle, out July 1.
story: How did Elle Woods become Elle Woods? A new Amazon Prime prequel series explores the childhood that shaped the “Legally Blonde” character, and the mother that made her.

In “Legally Blonde,” the 2001 movie that started a phenomenon, Elle’s mom is just a tiny role. June Diane Raphael imagines Elle’s mom, named Eva, as a put-together, practical woman focused on the social ladder.

“It’s limited real estate, so in a way, for an actor, it’s so great because you can kind of create and build the character yourself,” June Diane Raphael said of the original character in an interview with TODAY
Elle, played by Lexi Minetree, gets more than just blond hair from her mom, but also her confidence and savviness.

Prior to landing “Elle,” Minetree’s biggest credit was a guest appearance on the Season 26 premiere of “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.” She won over Reese Witherspoon, who originated the role and who produced the prequel through her company Hello Sunshine, with an audition tape.
With the exception of “Gilmore Girls,” Raphael tells TODAY.com most pop culture depictions of mother-daughter relationships don’t resonate with her.
“I think that so many representations of mothers and daughters in film and TV are a little odd,” Raphael says. “They’re filled with competition or weirdness.”
As Raphael explains, “Elle” turns that pattern on its head.
“I love playing this relationship that’s complicated and has its flaws, and sometimes they do the wrong thing, but it’s so fueled by love and admiration.”

Raphael has been vocal about what motherhood has meant to her, from the loss of her own mother when she was just 27 to raising her own two children, whom she shares with fellow comedian Paul Scheer. She tells TODAY.com what she hopes other mothers will take away from this expansion of a 90s film staple.

“My character rides so hard for her daughter,” Raphael says. “It’s really beautiful to see, and a lot of moms are going to resonate with that fact that we do anything, and sometimes that’s where we go wrong in a way, right?”

As a parent, Raphael thinks parents learn from kids if “you are awake from the experience.” Part of Season 1 sees Eva learning from her daughter and setting her up for Season 2, which she says allows Eva to explore who she is independent of her motherhood.

“So many women of that generation kind of looked up at a certain point, where the kids are getting older and maybe are a little bit more independent, and then they realize they’ve spent their whole life pouring everything into family and their husbands and kids, and then, what’s the next chapter for them?” Raphael says. “She realized a lot has been on hold, and so we get to explore what starts in the next chapter.”

title: Blake Lively Seeks $8 Million in Legal Fees in Justin Baldoni Dispute
summary: Blake Lively is seeking more than $8 million in attorneys’ fees and litigation costs from Justin Baldoni, his production company Wayfarer Studios, and the other parties she defeated in their now-dismissed $400 million defamation lawsuit.
story: Blake Lively is seeking more than $8 million in attorneys’ fees and litigation costs from Justin Baldoni, his production company Wayfarer Studios, and the other parties she defeated in their now-dismissed $400 million defamation lawsuit.

Lively accused Baldoni of sexual harassment during the production of their film“It Ends With Us,” which Baldoni directed and co-starred in. She also alleged that Wayfarer Studios retaliated against her after she complained about allegations of misconduct on the set of the film. Baldoni vehemently denied Lively’s claims.

The star first public with her allegations in December 2024, roughly four months after their film premiered in theaters. She first lodged a complaint with the California Civil Rights Department, then filed a federal lawsuit.

In a newly filed motion on Tuesday, Lively’s attorneys argue that Baldoni’s lawsuit was brought to punish Lively for reporting alleged sexual harassment and retaliation to California’s Civil Rights Department, rather than to pursue legitimate legal claims.

Her attorneys contend the defendants used the litigation to portray her as dishonest, intimidate potential witnesses, fuel a public relations campaign against her, and drive up the cost of her legal defense.

U.S. District Judge Lewis J. Liman tossed out most of Lively’s claims against Baldoni earlier this year, including harassment, defamation and conspiracy. The two parties reached a settlement deal in May.

Tuesday’s filing points to the court’s dismissal of the complaint, its finding that several claims were legally frivolous, and its ruling that Lively’s statements about the alleged misconduct were protected under California law.

Liman had dismissed Baldoni’s defamation and extortion lawsuit against Lively last year, but said she was allowed to move forward with a request for financial damages under California Civil Code Section 47.1, a law that protects people who report allegations of sexual misconduct from retaliatory defamation claims.

Lively’s legal team said the law requires reimbursement for the defense of the litigation because the legal work on the various claims was intertwined. They argue she is entitled to recover approximately $7,495,526.87 million in attorneys’ fees and another $539,514.01 in litigation expenses.

“Thanks to this landmark decision, those considering using a lawsuit as a weapon of intimidation have been put on notice that there are consequences for doing so,” Michael Gottlieb and Esra Hudson, Lively’s attorneys, said in a statement to NBC News. “The value of this ruling is in the precedent it creates, the accountability it imposes, and the protection it provides to those who may one day find themselves facing similar retaliation for speaking the truth.”

In the filing, the attorneys also defend the billing rates charged by her legal teams at Willkie Farr & Gallagher and Manatt, saying they were consistent with those typically charged in high-stakes, complex litigation.
The Wayfarer parties are expected to respond by July 13th.
Representatives for Baldoni did not immediately respond to request for comment on Tuesday.
This article first appeared on NBCNews.com.

title: What Kathie Lee Gifford Had to Say About Her Dating Life In New Interview
summary: For TODAY co-host Kathie Lee Gifford opened up in a new interview about romance and why she is enjoying single life in her 70s.
story: Kathie Lee Gifford is single and enjoying her life.

The longtime talk show personality and former TODAY co-host opened up in the cover story for the July 13 issue of People about how she views dating at 72 years old and the possibility of ever getting married again.

“I am not dating anybody right now, and I don’t want to date anybody,” she said. “I’m not looking, and I don’t think I’ll ever get married again. No, I don’t. I think I had an opportunity for that to maybe have happened, and it didn’t work out, so you move on. You stay friends if you can, and we have.”

Gifford said on TODAY in 2021 that she was in “a very special relationship” with a man whose name she did not divulge. However, Gifford shared with People in 2024 that she was no longer dating her mystery man.
She was previously married to Frank Gifford, a legendary New York Giants player and sports broadcaster, for 29 years before his death at 84 in 2015.
In her latest interview with People, also available on the People app, she did not completely shut the door on romance if the opportunity comes along.

“You know what it is? I leave room for the miraculous in my life. If God wants to do something miraculous to my life like give me another great love,” she said. “Frank will always be the love of my life. If you’re looking, then you’re looking for the love of the rest of your life.

“I need to find joy in the moment I’m in right now because none of us know when is our last breath,” she continued. “Instead of planning, ‘One day I’m going to take that vacation, one day this, my bucket list,’ that kind of thing, find joy right now in what you have already.”
The four-time Emmy winner and grandmother of five is more focused on what’s ahead.

“Because if you concentrate on everything you’ve lost and you live in the past — people who live in the past are doomed to die there,” she said. “And I don’t want to live in the past. I have been blessed for so many years, but I have great blessings today too, now that I’m back physically.”
Gifford shared that she had been in immense physical pain ahead of a hip replacement in 2024 and then pain in her other hip after she fell on Jan. 2 on the street outside her home.
She said she also broke her left arm while rolling over in bed in the middle of the night and underwent cataract surgery because her depth perception had been greatly affected.
“When I look back on all these years in this industry, I go, ‘I can’t believe I didn’t fall apart years ago,’” she said. “Your body starts to fall apart. And I never abused it, I just used it.”
She said she often stayed at home because she “didn’t want to go out like that” while experiencing chronic physical pain.
“I want to be Kathie Lee, the person they expect,” she said. “I don’t want to disappoint people.”
Gifford added that her vision is now 20/20 after cataract surgery, and she can be much more active with her grandchildren after stem cell treatments in her hip and arm.
“Now I’m in the season of the life where I don’t want to repeat myself,” she said. “I want to be remembered as somebody where if they only met me one time, she made me laugh, (and) she was kind.”

title: Read Paul Simon’s Letter for Clive Davis’ Funeral, Summing up 60 Years of Friendship
summary: A letter written by Paul Simon was read at the funeral for his close friend, music executive Clive Davis.
story: While Paul Simon wasn’t able to attend friend Clive Davis’ funeral, he made sure to honor the late music executive with a letter read aloud at the service.
Scores of stars turned out June 29 for the funeral of the legendary music executive, who died June 22 at the age of 94.

Kenny G performed a sax solo to kick off the event, held in New York City, while Dionne Warwick, Barry Manilow, Bruce Springsteen, Alicia Keys, Ja Rule and Stevie Wonder were also on hand, according to the Associated Press. Other luminaries, including Hoda Kotb, Adrien Brody, Nancy Pelosi and Gayle King, were also in attendance.

Davis, who won four Grammy Awards in his distinguished career, is known for launching and fostering the careers of some of the artists who attended his funeral as well as Whitney Houston, Aretha Franklin, Neil Diamond and more. He founded Arista Records and served as president of Columbia Records.

Simon, who was one of Davis’ longtime friends, wrote a letter that was read by Davis’ son Doug at the service, chronicling the relationship between the two musical heavyweights, both professionally and personally. Simon is currently on his “A Quiet Celebration Tour.”

“Beautiful moments happen when someone passes, if you can see them. One of those was reconnecting with that neighbor, Paul Simon,” Doug Davis said at the funeral, adding that his childhood best friend was Simon’s son Harper.

“I hadn’t spoken to Paul in 40 years. He and I have been able to speak every day this past week to reminisce and for me to receive some needed paternal advice and love,” Doug Davis added. “I finally had the chance to say something I’d wanted to say to him for 40 years. I told him when I was kid, he was just Harper’s dad. I had no idea the whole time he was Paul Simon.”
Read on for Simon’s full tribute to Clive Davis, provided to NBC News in full by the family.
Paul Simon’s Letter for Clive Davis’ Funeral

No one wants to find themselves speaking at a memorial for a dear friend. No one wants to piece together a chain of sentences that will inadequately express the shock of loss, the deep, sweet memories of times together, the love and admiration that was shared, and in my case, the closeness of our families.

When Doug called to tell me of his father’s passing, the name on my phone came up as Dougie Davis, Clive’s son. He then added that everyone in the world knows him now as Doug, but I would only think of him as Dougie, the kid who came to play with my son Harper in our apartment.

We were neighbors in the same building. His call made me think of the time Dougie and Harper were sitting at the kitchen table and l was mixing a chocolate milk for them. Harper accidentally tipped over Dougie’s glass. I said to him as l was cleaning up the mess, “You know, Harper, even if it’s an accident it’s still polite to tell your friend that you’re sorry.”
Harper said to Dougie, “Well I said, ‘Whoops-a-daisy.’”
I don’t think I ever told Clive that anecdote. So many stories, so many memories.

Clive and I were friends for nearly 60 years. Two New Yorkers from the boroughs who shared the kinship of a similar background. A lifelong friendship; always staying in touch and occasionally sharing a dinner or a summer afternoon.

With his loss, I now wish that we could have spent more time together. More time, more time. Comfortable, in each other’s company, conversation that was always interesting, ranging from music, to family, to politics and back to music.

Clive was a third of a trinity of record business deities: Mo Ostin, Ahmet Ertegun and Clive Davis. They shaped their labels around the artists. Leaders who changed the record industry. Men more interested in the music than popularity.

For a Harvard educated lawyer he had an uncanny grasp of the pulse of popular music. I remember the great anticipation that Art Garfunkel and I felt as we waited for Clive to hear “Bridge Over Troubled Water” for the first time. He sat immersed in the music and then turned to us and said, “That may be the most remarkable record I think I ever heard.” Or maybe I’m misremembering and he said, “What else you got?”
But I think he liked it.

A few weeks ago, my office got a message that Clive wanted to buy six seats to my upcoming concert at Forest Hills tennis stadium. The seats had to be dead center in the 10th row. When I play that night I’ll be singing for everyone, but in my heart I’ll be dedicating the night to the man in the empty seat, dead center in the 10th row.

title: ‘The Ring’ and ‘Lilo & Stitch’ Actor Daveigh Chase’s Cause of Death Revealed as AIDS
summary: The cause of death for Daveigh Chase, the actor known for her role in “The Ring” and voicing Lilo in the animated film “Lilo & Stitch,” has been revealed.
story: Daveigh Chase, the actor known for her role in “The Ring” and voicing Lilo in the animated film “Lilo & Stitch,” died from AIDS, according to the medical examiner report.

Chase, whose given name was Daveigh Schwallier, died in a Los Angeles hospital on June 16 at the age of 35. Her father, John Schwallier, confirmed to NBC News that she was homeless and living near the Los Angeles General Medical Center, where she died.
While The New York Times reported that Chase was living with her boyfriend, Schwallier said in a text message to NBC News that it was unclear what the man’s relationship was to his daughter.
“I don’t know how much of a boyfriend he was to her,” he said in a text message. “I seen a video of her in September. I don’t know why he wasn’t getting her medical help then.”
Daveigh Chase’s Cause of Death
Chase’s cause of death is listed as acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner’s report obtained by NBC News.
“Chronic polysubstance use” is also listed as a contributing factor. The report did not include what substances may have led to Chase’s death.
The manner is listed as natural. The case remains open.
Who is Daveigh Chase?
Chase was a child actor, whose first commercial was for Campbell’s Soup at age 7, according to IMDB.
Her breakout role was voicing Lilo in the animated film “Lilo & Stitch,” as well as the “Lilo & Stitch: The Series, “Stitch: The Movie” and various video games and spinoffs.

She was also known for being the child ghost Samira in “The Ring,” Samantha Darko in “Donnie Darko,” Rhonda Volmer in “Big Love” and had roles in “Mercy,” “CSI,” “Touched By An Angel” and “Family Law,” among others.
Her final acting credits are listed as 2016’s “American Romance” and “Jack Goes Home.”
What Is Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS)?
Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS) is a disease of the immune system caused by HIV, according to Clinicalinfo.

HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) is a virus that attacks cells that help fight infections, making the body vulnerable to life-threatening infections and cancers. If left untreated, it leads to AIDS.
Without medication, the lifespan of someone living with AIDS is about 3 years, HIV.gov reports. The time may be shorter depending on health factors.
What Is Chronic Polysubstance Use?
Chronic polysubstance use is when more two or more drugs are taken together, either intentionally or unintentionally, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Intentional polysubstance happens when a person takes a drug to increase or decrease the effects of a different drug or wants to experience the effects of the combination, the CDC reports. When it happens unintentionally, the person consuming the drug does not know it has been mixed or cut with other substances.

title: Lexi Minetree, the World’s New Elle Woods, Loves Video Games and the Color Green
summary: Lexi Minetree talks becoming Elle Woods for new Prime Video show “Elle” and how she’s different from the iconic character.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With Cut for Time, TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.

For those who grew up in the ’90s, there’s a throwback series coming to Prime Video in all its pink glory. “Elle,” a new prequel series to “Legally Blonde,” also has evergreen lessons to offer younger generations — and not just how to use a landline.
Lexi Minetree, 25, takes the helm in the show, portraying Elle Woods years before her famous pivot to practicing law.

With a self-proclaimed adrenaline buzz from her first-ever morning show appearance, Minetree walks into TODAY.com’s Orange Room with an infectious smile and sports a hot pink blazer suit set. As we sit down for more questions after her on-air chat with Savannah Guthrie and Carson Daly, she compliments my own pink jacket, with a fluffy pen from the June 20 “Elle World” New York City pop-up event clipped to the collar.
She tells me she approached her role with one primary question: How did the Elle Woods of “Legally Blonde” first get her confidence? She says “Elle,” out July 1 on Prime Video, answers it.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.

I feel like with the prequel, you really get to explore how does one get to not only learn who they are, but how to gain the confidence to be different, and to own what makes you you. I think, especially nowadays, bringing that sort of empowerment to a new generation of women, as well as the people who grew up loving “Legally Blonde,” I think that’s really special. Now you get eight more hours of this amazing character.

She says at least once a week people come up to her and go, “I became a lawyer because of this role,” or, “This character changed my life, or empowered me, or made me embrace who I was,” and that means something when a character is that special to someone. I hold that it is important to take care of things like that, and I think she really wanted to make sure that we captured her spirit. I’m really lucky because she really trusted me with this character.

It’s so funny that you say that, because there’s this website that has factoids on people, and my friend said to me, because there’s  trivia on it, the facts about me are that she’s a big fan of SpongeBob. I feel like there‘s a big culture of nonchalant-ness now, where people are afraid to make bold choices or lean into their interests in fear of being judged. I feel like getting to play Elle, I got to lean into all those things that in high school maybe I would have tried to hide a bit, and be someone who just embraces who they are and leans into the cringiness.

I feel like most people go method for crazy roles, but I feel like this character is one of the best characters to go method for, leaning into her character traits, which is being hardworking and believing in yourself ... I also want this character so ingrained in me that when I get to set, I can be free to make my own choices, because the script is so fun and the other actors I work with are so talented, that we throw stuff at each other all the time. There’s so much improvisation that happens on set, it kind of makes me sad that viewers only get to see one take of everything, because we do some crazy stuff, that I’m like, “I know this will never make it into the show,” but we sometimes just do it to make each other laugh. But more than that, too, there is some really heartfelt moments every episode, and I feel like that is what is so special about the show.

Oh, I really like that question. Thank you for asking. I actually feel like I’m a very different person than this character. I myself am not nearly as poised and well-dressed as I am today. This is thanks to my stylist.

I think when you play any character, you want to bring some of yourself to it. So, I feel like I have also been able to infuse myself. I think I’m a pretty goofy person. I try to not take myself so seriously, but I also feel like I’ve learned a lot from her. She’s so confident, and I think, especially as a young woman, sometimes you have self-doubt. Sometimes, you’re like, “Can I do this? Am I good enough?” And so I honestly, I’m thinking I’m trying to become more like her as a human being.
And before this, I’d never done comedy before, I did only drama work, so this was such a wonderful challenge for me.
OK, research!

Yeah, I did “Law and Order SVU,” which felt like the christening of becoming a New Yorker, and my character’s arc at the end, she became a lawyer. This is before the open call came out, so lots of weird kismet things. Like, “Universe, what are you up to?”

title: The Best Books to Read This Summer, According to Isaac Fitzgerald and Yasmine Cheyenne
summary: Here are six beach reads to read in 2026 according to Isaac Fitzgerald and Yasmine Cheyenne.
story: Is it summer, or is it summer reading season? Both answers are correct. If you’re not sure where to start on the books front, Isaac Fitzgerald and Yasmine Cheyenne stopped by TODAY on June 29 to share a few of the books they’re loving this season.

Yasmine Cheyenne, who is also a wellness coach and a meditation expert, is the author of “The Comeback Era,” provided a few books that will transport you to a less stressful place (hopefully). One is the latest offering from a Read With Jenna author Jessica George.
"The Comeback Era" by Yasmine Cheyenne
Welcome to your comeback era.
Isaac Fitzgerald, meanwhile, is the author of memoirs and most recently the travelogue “American Rambler: Walking the Trail of Johnny Appleseed.”
"American Rambler: Walking the Trail of Johnny Appleseed" by Isaac Fitzgerald
A heartwarming novel that tells Fitzgerald's story about following the steps of Johnny Appleseed.
Below, check out their picks.
Isaac’s Picks
"Phoebe Berman's Gonna Lose It" by Brooke Averick
A funny, warm story about a hopeless romantic determined to lose her virginity before her 30th birthday.

What Isaac said: “Phoebe Berman’s Gonna Lose It’ is oh so warm and deeply charming — a novel about romance, friendship, anxiety, and the strange little deadlines we invent for becoming ourselves. In this case, well, losing one’s virginity before turning 30. Laugh-out-loud funny while still being tender and big-hearted, here is a love story in the truest sense, about learning to want honestly, messily, and entirely on your own terms.”
"Main Characters: A Novel" by Bobby Palmer
A love story of a pair whose paths unexpectedly cross throughout two decades, told from outside perspectives.

What Isaac said: “Main Characters’ is a brilliant book — a captivating love story told from the margins by the people who perhaps understand us before we understand ourselves. The book follows Clara and Seb across two decades as their lives brush up against one another’s, but is told from the perspective of everyone around them. A clever concept that totally works, here is a great summer read for anyone who has ever believed in the life-changing power of truly being seen.”
"This Vast Enterprise: A New History of Lewis & Clark" by Craig Fehrman
After years of research, this is an entertaining history of US history's two famous explorers.

What Isaac said: “An incredible feat, Craig Fehrman’s ‘This Vast Enterprise’ is a wildly entertaining history of Lewis and Clark — the product of more than half a decade of rigorous and immensely impressive research — that never loses sight of the adventure at its center. Fehrman brings this legendary expedition thrillingly to life by turning our attention beyond Lewis and Clark themselves, revealing the oft-overlooked people and perspectives that made the journey possible. Expansive, compelling, and alive on every page, this is a perfect summer read for America’s 250th anniversary.”
Yasmine’s Picks
"The Art of Loving You" by Natasha Bishop
The sequel to Bishop's "Only for the Week" of an intimate, spicy romance set during a bucket list road trip.

What Yasmine said: “Impossible to put down, this romance winds you through love, loss and the joy thats possible on the other side of change. If you love a plot that moves you as much as it inspires you, this is your pick!’
"Love by the Book: A Novel" by Jessica George
An honest story about the complications of adult friendships and new connections.

What Yasmine said: “A page-turner that puts words to what so many of us quietly feel about adult friendships — the growing pains, the unexpected shifts, and the beauty of who finds you in the in-between.”
"Waiting on a Friend: A Novel" by Natalie Adler
Natalie Adler's debut novel.

What Yasmine said: “A debut that somehow makes you feel more alive the deeper it pulls you into loss — an absolute love letter to a moment in history that still echoes today, with all the heart and humor to prove it.”

title: Former ‘Love Island USA’ Star Alannah Keyser Draws Backlash For Apology Video After Dismissal From Show
summary: “Love Island USA” fans criticize former contestant Alannah Keyser’s newest apology for her previous use of a racial slur.
story: “Love Island USA” fans don’t seem to be buying former contestant Alannah Keyser’s newest apology for her previous use of a racial slur, which ultimately led to her dismissal from the show.

In a TikTok video on June 27, Keyser addressed a resurfaced clip, in which she was seen using a racial slur while singing the lyrics to the 2019 Roddy Rich song “The Box.” Keyser told viewers that the video was “from six years ago, and that word is just not in my vocabulary anymore.”
“I’m sorry to whoever saw that video and has been offended by it,” Keyser said in the TikTok video. “That was never my intention.”
Keyser, a 21-year-old film student from Miami, also said that she doesn’t support “racism or discrimination of any kind, and I never have.”
“This has definitely been a learning lesson for me, and it sucks that I didn’t get a chance to really show my personality and who I am,” she said.
Peacock did not have further comment on the issue.
The video has received thousands of comments from viewers, many of whom said they found her apology insufficient.
“Genuinely the worst apology I’ve ever seen,” said one TikTok user, who received more than 12,000 likes for the comment.

Keyser, who joined the show as a Casa Amor bombshell during the June 21 episode of the steamy series, stopped appearing on the program after the June 25 episode, Peacock confirmed to TODAY.com.
